subject: Order form: evidence & IP gating checklist
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novagrid.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novagrid.com, Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@novagrid.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form questions — evidence for IP & training opt-out

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement and legal at Novagrid reviewed sections 3.2–3.5 (IP / training / telemetry). Two quick asks before we kick this into our legal: 

1) Evidence: can you supply a one‑page summary of what evidence Redwood can provide to support the "no customer training" commitment (if we opt out) — things like audit logs, KV/cache retention policy, and a SOC2 extract that points to inference-only handling.
2) IP carveouts: the current redline gives us a "non‑exclusive license to use outputs" for productization. Our legal is pushing for explicit title/ownership in cases where output includes novelty. How flexible is Redwood on an explicit ownership handback for customer‑generated outputs?

We'd like to keep our procurement window open this month; legal said they'd be able to review if we have supporting evidence and a proposed clause alternative by Wednesday (2027-07-21). Can you confirm?

Attaching the order form PDF with their markups (OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Partnerships
Novagrid

Subject: Re: Order form questions — evidence for IP & training opt-out

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the annotated PDF. We've looped in legal (Irene) and Sales (Ben) to scope what we can provide and a short alternative clause for "title vs. license" scenarios.

Quick answers:
- Evidence packet: we can produce a 1‑page evidence summary + SOC2 extract + a short operator runbook excerpt. I’ll attach a draft evidence checklist by EOD tomorrow.
- Ownership: we typically offer a "license to use and productize" as standard. For cases where customers insist on title for specific outputs, we can propose a narrow handback (customer retains title to Customer Content + customer‑approved Derivative Outputs) but need procurement/legal confirmation on the operational implications (audit, segregation, and potential indemnities).

Proposed next steps (internal owners):
- Irene: produce redline language for (a) explicit customer title carveout for identified output artifacts and (b) training opt‑out assurances (logs/retention).
- Ben: align on commercial offset / one‑time fee if we need to provide title/handback for productized outputs.
- Laura (me): assemble evidence packet and a short cover note for Novagrid procurement.

We should be able to get everything to you by Wednesday (2027-07-21).

Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form questions — evidence for IP & training opt-out

Hi all — I reviewed Novagrid's comments and drafted a targeted redline and evidence summary. Key points: 

1) Evidence packet (brief):
- SOC2 Summary: we can provide the SOC2 summary page that covers processing and access controls (SOC2_Summary.xlsx attached).
- Inference handling statement: a 1‑page statement confirming that when a customer selects "no training / no feedback ingestion" the runtime discards ephemeral KV cache per retention policy and no training datasets are recorded.
- Audit hooks: we can provide request/response logs (redacted PII) for a 90‑day window on request and a sample trace showing routing/fallback behavior.

2) Ownership options and proposed language (high level):
- Standard: non‑exclusive, perpetual license to use Outputs for productization.
- Customer title carveout (narrow): customer may request assignment of title to "Customer Created Outputs" where the output is derived solely from Customer Content and a deterministic transformation — provided customer: (a) identifies artifacts with unique IDs at time of creation, (b) accepts operational constraints (separate export bundle), and (c) executes a limited assignment addendum.

Operational implications: title assignment triggers an export/forensics workflow, a one‑time engineering verification, and an elevated procurement fee to cover evidence collation and storage. We propose a process: customer flags requests within 30 days of output creation; Redwood produces an export pack within 15 business days; fee applies (to be commercialized by Ben).

See attached: Legal_Redlines_20270719.docx (docx) with inline comments and the draft clause labeled "CustomerCreatedOutputAssignment".

I recommend the following immediate language to include in the order form as an appendix (short): 
"If Customer requests title assignment for specified Outputs, Parties will execute an Assignment Addendum and Redwood will provide an export bundle and verification within agreed timelines. Assignment applies only to Outputs comprised solely of Customer Content and will be subject to a one‑time operational fee."

Happy to walk through this with Novagrid legal if they'd like a quick sync.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Legal_Redlines_20270719.docx (docx); SOC2_Summary.xlsx (xlsx)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial note on title carveout & evidence fees

Elena / Novagrid procurement —

Thanks for raising this. Quick commercial framing from our side: we can offer the narrow title assignment workflow Irene outlined, with the following commercial guardrails: 

- Operational fee: one‑time fee of USD 15,000 per assignment request to cover verification, export, and secure storage.
- SLA for export/verification: 15 business days for the initial export bundle, 30 business days for deep forensic verifications (if requested).
- Training opt‑out: no recurring fee; if Novagrid elects to opt out of feedback/training ingestion we provide the evidence packet at no additional cost (SOC2 excerpt + runbook + trace sample).

If this commercial structure works for Novagrid, I'll ask procurement to confirm the fee and we can incorporate the Assignment Addendum into the order form. If Novagrid prefers a standing blanket title assignment for all outputs (not anticipated), we'll need a different commercial model.

Laura/Markus/Neha: please flag anything I missed.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
